starting_principles: Newton's Second Law for center-of-mass translational motion: F_net = M a_cm
Newton's Second Law for rotation about center of mass: tau_cm = I_cm alpha
Kinematic pure rolling constraint: a_cm = R alpha
assumptions: Rigid symmetrical body (circular cross-section of radius R, mass M, centroidal inertia I_cm = M k^2)
Inclined plane of constant angle theta with horizontal
Sufficient static friction at contact point to prevent slipping (f_s <= mu_s N)
Zero rolling resistance and zero aerodynamic drag

ordered_steps.description: Formulate linear equation of motion down the incline
ordered_steps.operation: Resolve gravity component M g sin(theta) down incline and static friction f_s up incline
assumptions_applied: Direction of static friction opposes downward impending slip at contact point

ordered_steps.description: Formulate rotational equation of motion about center of mass
ordered_steps.operation: Evaluate torques about CM: gravity and normal force pass through CM (zero torque), friction provides torque f_s R
assumptions_applied: Center of mass is geometric center of symmetric rolling body

ordered_steps.description: Apply the pure rolling no-slip kinematic constraint
ordered_steps.operation: Express angular acceleration in terms of linear acceleration: alpha = a_cm / R
assumptions_applied: Zero relative velocity at contact point (no slipping)

ordered_steps.description: Substitute friction expression into the translational equation of motion
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute f_s = (I_cm / R^2) a_cm and group acceleration terms
ordered_steps.result_equation: M g \sin\theta - \frac{I_{\text{cm}}}{R^2} a_{\text{cm}} = M a_{\text{cm}} \implies M g \sin\theta = \left( M + \frac{I_{\text{cm}}}{R^2} \right) a_{\text{cm}}

ordered_steps.description: Solve for linear acceleration and express using radius of gyration
ordered_steps.operation: Divide by M (1 + I_cm / (M R^2)) and substitute I_cm = M k^2
assumptions_applied: Definition of radius of gyration k^2 = I_cm / M

ordered_steps.description: Determine required friction force and critical static friction coefficient
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute a_cm into f_s expression and impose Coulomb inequality
ordered_steps.result_equation: f_s = \frac{M g \sin\theta}{1 + \frac{M R^2}{I_{\text{cm}}}} \le \mu_s M g \cos\theta \implies \mu_s \ge \mu_{\min} = \frac{\tan\theta}{1 + \frac{M R^2}{I_{\text{cm}}}} = \frac{\tan\theta}{1 + \frac{R^2}{k^2}}
assumptions_applied: Normal reaction balance N = M g cos(theta)
Static friction limit f_s <= mu_s N

applicability_conditions: Valid strictly for pure rolling without slipping (mu_s >= mu_min)
If mu_s < mu_min, body slips and accelerates at a = g(sin theta - mu_k cos theta) with alpha = mu_k M g cos(theta) R / I_cm
source_references: H.C. Verma Vol 1, Chapter 10, Section 10.17 (Rolling on an Inclined Plane)
